summary_oneline: Raise the google-genai floor and refresh GoogleModel for Gemini 4.x (Argon), retiring deprecated ids

localization.role: the model catalogue itself — 53 names, 34 distinct values
Vertex subset, no aliases, separate decision
the precedent shape for retiring ids
public HTTP surface enumerating the enum

constraints.claim: Duplicate enum values become aliases, so a 4.x name reusing an existing value vanishes and the public catalogue publishes 34 ids, not 53
Capability routing is by string prefix, not enum membership — a gemini-4 id silently takes the conservative two-phase path
Google declares no deprecated_models, so LLMFactory always reports an empty deprecated list for it; OpenAI's DEPRECATIONS is the in-repo precedent
Only two distributions pin google-genai and they disagree (>=2.23.0 vs >=2.18.1); installed is 2.24.0 and google-cloud-aiplatform couples the floor
handlers/google_generation.py publishes the enum over HTTP, so removals are a visible API change
Three test modules assert exact name->value pairs and fail on any removal
The same operation was done twice before with a stable 3-part footprint: enum + prefix whitelist + tests
A gemini-4 id inherits the 1M compaction window automatically via the bare gemini- prefix

changes.what: GoogleModel / VertexAIModel: add the 4.x (Argon) members, retire the deprecated ones
client.py: extend _default_combined_call_prefixes, _requires_thinking, _is_gemini3_model and the _default/_fallback/_lightweight/_reformat ids for the new family
Introduce GoogleGenAIClient.deprecated_models following the OpenAI DEPRECATIONS shape so retirement is expressible
Raise the google-genai floor in ai-parrot-client-google and realign ai-parrot-embeddings
Update the three test modules that pin model ids

non_goals: Rewriting the prefix-gate design into capability metadata on the enum
Moving the Google model tests out of packages/ai-parrot/tests into the satellite
Touching parrot/clients/base.py or the LLMFactory contract
Vertex-specific location/api_version plumbing beyond adding members

risks.risk: Adding 4.x to the enum without touching the prefix gates ships a silently degraded path (no combined tools+schema, wrong thinking config)
Deleting ids breaks the public /models response and three test modules
A 4.x name reusing an existing value becomes an invisible alias

confidence_map.claim: The catalogue is models.py in ai-parrot-client-google
19 of 53 names are enum aliases; only 34 distinct values
A deprecated_models seam exists and Google does not use it
The enum is published over HTTP and pinned by three test modules
The precedent footprint is enum + whitelist + tests (2 prior commits)
A gemini-4 id inherits the 1M compaction window with no edit
Which ids to ADD (Gemini 4.x Argon) is unknown
Which ids to RETIRE is unknown
The target google-genai version is unknown

unknowns.question: What are the exact Gemini 4.x (Argon) model ids to add, and what google-genai version is the floor?
How should deprecated ids be retired: delete them, remap them as aliases (current Google practice), or introduce a GoogleGenAIClient.deprecated_models registry in the OpenAI DEPRECATIONS shape?
Does the 4.x family go into _default_combined_call_prefixes, and is any 4.x Pro thinking-only (_requires_thinking)?
Do _default_model / _fallback_model / _lightweight_model / _default_reformat_model move to 4.x now, or stay on 3.x until Argon is GA?
Does VertexAIModel receive the 4.x family in the same change?

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and the footprint is a known, twice-executed shape; what is missing is operator-supplied data (model ids, SDK floor) and one design decision (how to express retirement), both of which a spec resolves. No architectural fork justifies a brainstorm.
